intro: On the İslahiye plain, in Gaziantep province, rises Tilmen Höyük, a mound whose story reaches back to the 3rd millennium BC. In the second millennium BC it was the capital of a city state. Its basalt-footed palace and gate have been re-erected, and you can walk right through them.
history: In the second millennium BC this mound was the capital of a city state, and it reflects the region's position between Aleppo and the Hittite world. Italian and Turkish excavations uncovered its basalt-footed palace and its monumental gate. Both have now been re-erected, and both are open for you to walk through.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the palace, the monumental gate, the basalt column bases and the city walls.
facts: Did you know? This is one of the few archaeological parks where the finds were re-erected in place, so you see walls rather than foundations. In the second millennium BC the mound was the capital of a city state, standing between Aleppo and the Hittite world.
outro: This brings our journey through Tilmen Höyük to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
